# CANDIDATE: RSI_STRUCTURE_DIVERGENCE_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

Bullish RSI divergence (price makes a higher low while RSI makes a lower low) combined with a structural higher low in price and an aligned bullish EMA ribbon (5>8>13) signals an upcoming upward move. The setup aims to capture mean-reversion bounces in choppy to low-trend regimes (VIX 15-25) during midday when momentum wanes.

## Mechanism

Entry: At the close of the second low bar when:  
1. Price forms a higher low (HL) relative to the prior swing low.  
2. RSI(14) forms a lower low (LL) on those two lows (bullish divergence).  
3. Price is above the 20-period EMA ribbon, defined as 5-EMA > 8-EMA > 13-EMA.  
4. Volume on the second low bar exceeds the 20-bar average volume.  

Exit: Initial stop at the low of the divergence bar (the second low bar). Target at 1.5R (risk-reward). After TP1 is hit, trail the remaining position with a chandelier exit (ATR × 3). Only trade between 10:00-14:00 ET and when VIX is between 15 and 25; avoid strong trend mornings and VIX <12.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The strategy assumes a minimum account size of $25K to trade the default qty of 28 contracts (based on risk-per-trade of 50% and typical entry premium ~$1.80). A $1K paper account would realize approximately 14% of headline P&L (qty ~4 contracts).  
2. **Sample bias:** The hypothesis is derived from conceptual technical analysis; no historical sample has been evaluated yet. Sample size is zero, selection method is none, overfit risk is high until a Stage-1 backtest is performed.  
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward or held-out window tested).  
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no realistic OPRA simulation on top 3 J days).  
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: entering during a strong trend breakout could lead to repeated stop-outs as price continues against the divergence signal; max drawdown could exceed 50% of account if multiple consecutive losses occur; blow-up scenario: trading in low VIX (<12) where divergence signals are unreliable and stops are tight, leading to slippage and catastrophic loss.  
6. **Concentration:** Unknown until backtest; if the strategy relies on a few anomalous days, concentration could exceed 100% of P&L.
